fields.meta_description: Describe your approval limits and pay days. Emergent builds accounts payable automation that matches each invoice to its PO. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Accounts Payable Automation From Inbox to Paid
fields.hero_description: Describe who signs off at which amount and the day you pay suppliers. Emergent builds the app that runs your AP inbox on those rules, and changes it when the policy does.
fields.features_subheading: With accounts payable automation, no one retypes an invoice, and people see only the bills that break one of your rules.
fields.feature_1:
Invoice capture from email and uploads

A PDF in the AP inbox or an upload from a vendor portal is read into fields: vendor, invoice number, due date and each line item. Low-confidence fields wait for a person.
fields.feature_2:
Two-way and three-way matching

Service invoices are checked against the PO, and goods invoices against the receipt too. A bill for a partial delivery matches what has arrived, and the rest of the PO stays open.
fields.feature_3:
Approval routing by amount and vendor

Bills route by amount, vendor, entity, or GL code, and the request lands in Slack or email. A reminder follows after two days. A missed deadline escalates to a backup approver.
fields.feature_4:
Payment runs on your schedule

Approved bills are batched into a weekly run, and nothing leaves until someone in finance releases it. The run then goes out as a bank file or through the payments API you connect.
fields.feature_5:
Posted to your accounting system

Each approved bill posts to QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite with its GL code and a link back to the source PDF. Once a payment run is released, each payment posts against its bill.
fields.feature_6:
Code in your repo, data in your database

The matching rules and approval chain export to your GitHub repository, where an engineer can read exactly why a bill was held. Bill and payment records stay in a database you own.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your AP Automation With Emergent?
fields.why_description: In an AP suite, your approval rules live inside the vendor's app. With Emergent they are code in your repo, changed by prompting.

fields.usecase_heading: AP Automation Workflows to Build Today
fields.tab_content_1:
Match every invoice to its PO before it reaches an approver

Northwind's invoice is matched line by line to PO-3107 and the goods receipt, and any price or quantity outside the tolerance holds it. The fasteners are billed at $0.43 against $0.40, and the $60.00 difference goes to Dana Kim, the buyer, to approve or dispute. Clean matches go to the budget owner, then post to NetSuite.
fields.tab_content_2:
Pay recurring bills on time without a reminder spreadsheet

Rent and software subscriptions come in every month, and each bill is compared with the one before it. When the design tool bill jumps to $1,980 from $1,650, a rise of more than 10%, it waits for Priya Shah, the department head. Everything else goes straight into Friday's payment run.
fields.tab_content_3:
Give every entity its own approver and bank account

The bill-to address on an invoice decides which company it belongs to, and the bill goes to that entity's controller for approval. Acme Ltd pays its bills from the GBP account and Acme GmbH from the EUR account. One dashboard splits the month's spend by entity for the close.
fields.tab_content_4:
Pay contractors once their paperwork is complete

Contractors invoice from a phone, and the hours are checked against the contract rate. The W-9 and bank details are collected once, verified on every submission and kept with each payment for 1099 reporting. Jordan Lee's invoice for 30 hours at $80 joins the biweekly Friday payout on Oct 23.

fields.howto_description: The first three steps are decisions finance makes before anyone opens Emergent. The last four turn those decisions into a working app.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Map how invoices reach you today
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the approval rules in writing
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every way invoices arrive today: the shared AP inbox, paper bills scanned at the front desk, and contractor emails sent to whoever hired them. Note who touches each one and where it waits. That map becomes the intake and the first routing rules.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe the policy the way your controller would say it: anything over $10,000 goes to the CFO, and a new software vendor needs procurement first. Add the exceptions too, such as capital purchases that need the board at any amount. Emergent turns those sentences into routing rules.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose two-way matching for services and three-way matching for goods you receive. Then set the price tolerance and the quantity tolerance separately. A tight tolerance catches more overbilling and sends more invoices back to buyers. The test in step 6 shows where yours belongs.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the ledger your team closes the books in, such as QuickBooks or any ERP with an API. The vendor list and open purchase orders sync in first. GL code suggestions then come from how your team coded the same vendor's past bills.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the weekday your regular run goes out and the account it draws from. Terms of 2/10 net 30 give 2% off for paying within 10 days, which is $240 on a $12,000 invoice. Bills on those terms can go into an early-pay run before the discount lapses.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last month's invoices through the automated AP workflow before go-live. Wherever its route or GL code differs from what your team did by hand, fix the rule by prompting and run the sample again until every decision agrees.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live and watch cycle time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Point the AP inbox at the workflow and keep the old process as a fallback for one payment cycle. On the dashboard, watch the days each invoice takes to get paid and the share of bills held. A hold rate that keeps rising usually means a tolerance is too tight.

specificity.evidence: AP vocabulary throughout: "Service invoices are checked against the purchase order, and goods invoices against the receipt as well", "A vendor offering 2/10 net 30 can go into an early-pay run before the tenth day", "an approved invoice becomes a vendor bill linked to its purchase order, with the subsidiary and department set by your rules". openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence with a verb: "A PDF in the AP inbox or an upload from a vendor portal is read into fields", "Bills route by amount, vendor, entity, or GL code", "Rent and software subscriptions arrive as recurring bills.", "List every way invoices arrive today". No label openers, no verbless feature bodies (rows 2 and 16 clear).

craft.evidence: One rule is stated three times across body fields, with words swapped so QC Q6 misses it (row 18 class, body to body): (1) feature_2 "A price or count outside your tolerance holds the bill for the buyer." (2) tab_content_1 "A price or quantity outside the tolerance holds it." (3) howto_step_3_des "set how far a unit price or a received quantity may drift from the PO before the invoice is held for the buyer." Same class, second idea: hero_description "Describe who signs off at which amount and the day you pay suppliers" is restated by howto_description "who approves what, how much variance you accept, and when suppliers get paid" (the meta mirroring the hero is fine; the how-to intro should not be a third telling). FIX: keep the general tolerance rule in step 3 and the tab 1 story phrase (I4 needs it); give feature_2 a second sentence that says something new, such as what the hold shows the buyer (the line, the PO price and the variance). Rewrite howto_description so it says what this how-to adds rather than relisting the hero's inputs. No ", so" tails (0), 3 from-X-to-Y ranges, no sentence over 32 words: rows 4, 6 and 19 clear.

voice.evidence: (1) tab_content_1 "and the buyer gets the $60.00 difference" reads as if the buyer is paid $60. The image says "Sent to Dana Kim, buyer / Approve the difference or dispute it". FIX: "and the $60.00 difference goes to the buyer to approve or dispute" (keep "the $60.00 difference" for the I4 story link). A bill that rises by more than a tenth waits for the department head. The rest join Friday's payment run without a review." tab_content_4 has the same four-beat shape and closes on a summary line: "Every payment record stays ready for 1099 season." (3) howto_step_7_des ends on a tacked-on line unrelated to the step: "Every rule change is versioned in your repo." (see also truth). (4) howto_step_4_des "Connect the ledger your team closes the books in, QuickBooks or any ERP with an API." The comma appositive reads as a splice; use "such as QuickBooks or any ERP with an API". Accepted P2, not part of this fail: tab 2 "rises by more than a tenth" in place of 10% follows the pending C3 decision.

truth.evidence: howto_step_7_des "Every rule change is versioned in your repo." states platform behaviour as automatic (row 14). The ledger's code-export entry is only "Full code export to the user's GitHub repository"; it does not say each change is committed or versioned. FIX: drop the sentence, or reword within the ledger, e.g. "Export the rules to your repo after each change and review them like any other code." Everything else checks out. All 10 claims_used ids are approved. FAQ 3 vendor descriptions and the table match the library (BILL/Tipalti settled). The numbers agree: 400 x $8 = $3,200; 2,000 x $0.43 = $860; $3,200 + $860 + $340 = $4,400; 2,000 x $0.03 = $60; $0.43 vs $0.40 is 7.5%, over the mockup's 2%; $1,650 to $1,980 = +$330 = 20%, over 10%; 14 bills / $38,210 match on tab 2 and the cover; $80 x 30 = $2,400. Oct 23, 2026 is a Friday, Nov 18 a Wednesday. Rows 7, 8, 12 and 13 clear ("Design tool subscription", no real brand).

Capture is sent to invoice automation (FAQ 5 "For capture and matching on their own, see invoice automation") and sign-off only to approval workflow (FAQ 9 "If sign-off is all you need, start with an approval workflow"). faq.evidence: 10 on-topic items, the hub link in item 2, and 3 exact-match sibling links. Three answers still fail. Each sentence becomes a step in the workflow it builds" repeats howto_step_2_des "Describe the policy the way your controller would say it... Emergent turns those sentences into routing rules". "Before go-live, set every threshold in the generated approval chain beside your written policy" repeats howto_step_6_des "Run last month's invoices through the automated AP workflow before go-live and set its decisions beside what your team did by hand". FIX: answer "How do you automate accounts payable?" with the order of work (intake, rules, matching, ledger, payment, test) in two sentences that point to the how-to, or with something the steps do not cover. (2) FAQ 5 "A field read with low confidence, like a smudged invoice number on a scan, goes to a person first" restates feature_1 "Low-confidence fields wait for a person." The smudge example is new, but the claim is not. FIX: keep the example and cut the restated rule, or answer with what happens after the match. (3) FAQ 10 "ask each of the AP automation companies to show it working" is shoehorned to fit the secondary; a person would write "ask each vendor". FIX: place "AP automation companies" where it reads naturally, e.g. "Most AP automation companies will run a demo on sample data; bring your own approval chain instead...".
